preview.end.exited: {known, select, yes {The dev server exited (code {code}).} other {The dev server exited.}}
preview.end.notListening: Nothing listened on port {port} within {seconds} s.
preview.end.otherPort: The server listens on {ports}, not on {port}: pass the port it is given, such as --port %PORT%.
preview.end.placeEnded: Stopped: its slot's lease or its review ended.
preview.end.placeHeld: An earlier dev server here couldn't be ended, so nothing starts here until it is.
preview.end.projectClosed: Stopped: the project or its workspace closed.
preview.end.stranger: Port {port} is held by another program (process {pid}), so its page isn't shown.
preview.end.turnedOff: Stopped: the Preview was turned off.
preview.settings.address: Each start gets a free port from {first}–{last} in {variable}. The server must listen on it on localhost: the page is then at {url}.
preview.settings.badPath: A page path starts with / and has no spaces or backslashes.
preview.settings.hmr: A second port for hot reload
preview.settings.hmrNote: In {variable}, for a server whose hot reload socket listens apart.
preview.settings.noSuggestion: No dev, start or preview script in package.json to suggest.
preview.tab.about: The page runs in a guarded view of its own: it reaches only its own dev server and the internet over https, never this computer's other services or your network, and asks for no permissions. The dev server's command is yours and runs with your rights. Turn the Preview off in Settings → Advanced (Preview: run projects' dev servers).
preview.tab.failed: Couldn't do that in the Preview
preview.tab.notStarted: The dev server isn't running here. Start runs {command}.
preview.tab.setUp: Set the command that runs this project's dev server in Project Settings → Preview, and the Preview tab shows its page here.
preview.tab.stale: stale: its files changed after it started
